pr_title: Feature: Initial assortment of refactor changes for review
pr_body:
TBD

Closes #3342

(Obviously, do not merge these)
pr_comments:
Cannot give huge useful feedback on the refactoring as a whole aside that it looks very promising.

The work on regrouping the different commands in `IItemCommandService.cs` is a very good idea. 

Been only playing with commands around the recycle bin, one can feel there is a lot of convoluted code around creating new commands. Something here begs to be streamlined.

Even if the behaviors are slightly different depending from where we're coming (Sidebar / Former IShellPage for exemple), maybe it'd be possible to create a common base for each command? This refactor gives a small starting ground for it at least.

Looks like my code selection for the review has been a bit messy... Hope you'll be able to make something out of it @lukeblevins.

If some modifications I suggested look good to you but you don't have time for them, hit me up and I'll see what I can do!

First code review for me as well on Git, if you've got any feedback, I'll take it!
I think the #10185 is partially adressed in this refactoring.

issue_context.title: Feature: Add the ability to close the primary/left panel
issue_context.body:
**Requirements**
- Add support for closing the left pane
comments:
See #2941 for a similar request.
Adding an option to close the left pane is more complicated as the left pane is the "main pane" and the sidebar is part of it, I'm keeping this open a feature request for this.

> See #2941 for a similar request. Adding an option to close the left pane is more complicated as the left pane is the "main pane" and the sidebar is part of it, I'm keeping this open a feature request for this.

@gave92 can we decouple the sidebar from the panes?
That statement in not true anymore, Sidebar is now part of MainPage.
Is this an issue in the preview version? https://files.community/download/preview

Yes, but I think it'll be resolved with #10161

@lukeblevins can you confirm?
@yaira2 Can confirm that's in the works. 👍🏻
Now this is feasible by introducing the new sidebar control? @yaira2

> Now this is feasible by introducing the new sidebar control? @yaira2

If the Sidebar is closed entirely, we can lock it into the Minimal mode regardless of break points, and the toggle to display it can be visible in the address bar all the time.
@yaira2 How, do you think, is this gonna be achieved? I've been thinking about adding a setting to minimalize to a toggle button on the tabbar.
We're actively working on the foundation for this feature.
I’m excited to share that this enhancement will be included in the upcoming v3.5 release.

review_comments: Feels weird to have an empty `else if` statement. Nothing can be done to remove it?
This condition is repeated at least five times in this file only. Worth wrapping it up in a method explicitely named to tell what it does.
Those different keywords are used in several places. Maybe it could be worth to change them into some `public const string` stored inside `Constants.cs ` ?
The keywords will go away soon once we drop the FullTrust component :)
This expression is used several times through the file. Wrapping it up in a method would be worth.
Several of those constructs are repeated in the code. Maybe a method to regroup their creation into one method taking arguments to customize the message in Entry could be worth the trouble to set up?

There are several classes that are using a combination of arguments of type `(IStorageItem source, string destination, NameCollisionOption collision, IProgress<float> progress, IProgress<FileSystemStatusCode> errorCode, CancellationToken cancellationToken)`.

To be honest, this is such an eyesoar to read and so much repetition. Any possibility to wrap those objects into a class / structure ? Something of the likes of  `public class FileSystemOperationArguments` for example?
